name: g02-01 EBITDA L2 growth-ROIC-reinvestment twins
mechanism: EV/EBITDA ignores capital expenditure, so two firms with identical growth and ROIC but different capex needs convert EBITDA to free cash flow at very different rates and deserve different multiples. Adding capex intensity to the growth, ROIC, leverage and size match of the best generation-1 recipe, inside a 2-digit industry that shares macro risk, should pick peers whose free-cash-flow conversion and therefore warranted EV/EBITDA most closely match the target.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.325 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with coverage of at least 99%.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

name: g02-02 EBITDA cross-industry fundamental twins
mechanism: A steady-state DCF ties EV/EBITDA to growth, the reinvestment rate needed to fund it (capex intensity and ROIC), and risk (leverage and size), not to the SIC code itself. Taking nearest neighbours on these drivers from the whole cross-section lets the peers be much closer on fundamentals than an industry list allows, the same effect that made cross-industry matching work for EV/Sales.
prediction: Median error below the 0.333 industry baseline and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 1, ebitda_margin 0.5, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=3

name: g02-03 EBITDA narrow industry ranked on growth and capex
mechanism: Narrow 3-digit industry peers share technology and demand shocks, and within that set the remaining dispersion in EV/EBITDA comes mostly from growth expectations and how much capex is needed to sustain them. A larger minimum peer count with cascading fallbacks keeps the median stable when the narrow industry is thin.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.330 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.

spec.name: g02-03 EBITDA narrow industry ranked on growth and capex

compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 1, roic 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

name: g02-04 Sales cross-industry margin band plus growth and capex
mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so a tight hard band on EBITDA margin removes the dominant source of error, and EV/EBITDA in turn depends on growth and capex needs. Drawing peers from all industries inside the margin band, then ranking on margin, gross margin, growth and capex intensity, matches both factors of the identity.
prediction: Median error below 0.410 and beats the industry median in all 4 years, with coverage of at least 98%.

spec.name: g02-04 Sales cross-industry margin band plus growth and capex

compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.03 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.06] -> []

name: g02-05 Sales L2 with margin band, robust median
mechanism: Within a 2-digit industry, firms share risk and business model, and a hard EBITDA-margin band guarantees comparable profitability, the main driver of EV/Sales. The broader L2 pool (rather than L3) leaves more candidates inside the band, and ranking on margin and growth with a median aggregator gives a stable estimate.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.415 and beats the industry median in all 4 years.

spec.name: g02-05 Sales L2 with margin band, robust median

compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.04 | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, capex_intensity 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.04] -> []

name: g02-06 Sales profitability-dominant twins, trimmed mean
mechanism: Because EV/Sales is EBITDA margin times EV/EBITDA, the margin match should dominate, with growth, capex intensity and leverage acting as secondary determinants of the EV/EBITDA factor. A larger peer set aggregated by trimmed mean averages out idiosyncratic valuation noise while discarding extreme multiples.
prediction: Median error below 0.420 and beats the industry median in all 4 years with 100% coverage.

spec.name: g02-06 Sales profitability-dominant twins, trimmed mean

compact: EV/Sales | rank ebitda_margin 3, sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, capex_intensity 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5 | k=15, trimmed_mean, min_peers=3
